description: The bar chart illustrates the sample counts for four essay genres—Argumentative, Narrative, Descriptive, and Expository—categorized by two conditions: “Open” (light blue) and “Cons.” (light pink), likely short for “Constrained,” as indicated in the legend. The vertical axis, labeled “Sample Count,” ranges from 0 to 130 in increments of 20. For each genre, two adjacent bars represent the sample sizes under each condition. In the Argumentative genre, the Open condition has 79 samples and the Cons. condition has 122. For Narrative, Open has 80 and Cons. has 87. In Descriptive, Open has 68 and Cons. has 100. Finally, in Expository, Open has 62 and Cons. has 130. Across all genres, the Cons. condition consistently has a higher sample count than the Open condition, with the largest difference observed in the Expository genre (68 samples more) and the smallest in Narrative (7 samples more). The bars are grouped by genre along the horizontal axis, with no sorting applied, and each bar is labeled with its exact numerical value at the top. The chart visually emphasizes the disparity between conditions within each genre, with the Cons. bars uniformly taller than their Open counterparts.
